Chapter 01 Reading 1 다리 둘 달린 당근, 먹어도 될까?
Have you ever seen a carrot with two legs?
Or a pumpkin covered in big warts?
These are called “ugly” vegetables.
Many people think they’re not fresh or tasty because of how they look.
So stores refuse to sell them, and tons of food go to waste.
This means farmers lose time, money, and valuable crops.
This food waste also harms the environment.
When vegetables rot, they release a greenhouse gas that causes climate change.
To fix these problems, some online stores now sell ugly vegetables at lower prices.
They want people to try them and see that appearance doesn’t affect taste or nutrients.
By buying these vegetables, people can support farmers, save money, and help the environment.
So, next time you see a strange vegetable, give it a try.
It might be the best one you’ve ever eaten!
Chapter 01 Reading 2 우유가 치즈로 변한 놀라운 사건
Cheese is a food enjoyed worldwide, but no one knows exactly where it first came from.
One story says that early nomads discovered it by accident.
While they traveled under the hot sun, they carried milk in bags made from animal stomachs.
After a long journey, the nomads opened the bags and found something surprising.
The milk was no longer liquid, but thick and soft lumps.
It had turned into cheese!
What caused this change?
Most likely, the milk changed due to a natural enzyme in the animal stomachs.
And the heat from the sun probably made this process happen faster.
The nomads found that the cheese tasted good and lasted longer than milk.
Soon, people everywhere began making cheese on purpose.
This lucky discovery gave us one of our favorite foods.
Chapter 01 Reading 3 동물을 죽이지 않고 만드는 고기
There is a way to make meat without killing animals.
It is called lab-grown meat.
Scientists take a few cells from an animal and put them in a special tank.
Inside, the cells are given nutrients that help them grow, just like in a real animal.
After a few weeks, they become muscle.
Scientists collect these pieces of muscle and combine them.
Then, the combined pieces are processed into meat products such as burger patties or chicken nuggets.
Lab-grown meat could change the future of food.
However, there are still some problems to solve.
The production process is expensive because the equipment and nutrients cost a lot.
It is also challenging to make large amounts, as the cells need very controlled conditions to grow.
In addition, some people feel uneasy about eating meat grown in a lab.
Even so, many scientists and companies are working to improve the process.
Their efforts could one day make lab-grown meat a common food on our tables.
Chapter 01 Reading 4 샌드위치가 우주 음식을 바꾼 이유
In 1965, astronaut John Young brought a sandwich to space.
After taking one bite, crumbs flew everywhere.
This incident helped NASA realize the danger of crumbs.
Without gravity, crumbs float through the air.
These tiny pieces can get into machines or an astronaut’s nose and cause serious problems.
That’s why modern space food is made to stay in one piece.
Foods such as rice and pasta are dried and packaged in sealed bags.
Astronauts add water to them before eating.
Salt and pepper are made into liquids and put in small bottles.
And instead of bread, astronauts eat tortillas because they’re soft and don’t make crumbs.
When eating in space, safety comes first!
Chapter 02 Reading 1 중국이 판다를 다른 나라에 보내는 이유
When people think of animals from China, pandas are often the first to come to mind.
Pandas are rare and live only in China.
So the country sends them to zoos in other nations as a sign of friendship.
This is known as panda diplomacy.
When pandas arrive in a new country, they quickly win people’s hearts.
Many people fall in love with these gentle animals.
As people learn more about pandas, they can also learn more about China and its culture.
This helps them see the country in a more positive way.
Panda diplomacy also lets countries work closely with China.
Zoos in other countries work with Chinese experts to care for the pandas.
By working together, they build trust and understanding between their countries.
Chapter 02 Reading 2 죽음 앞에서 코끼리는 어떻게 행동할까?
Humans feel sadness when loved ones die, but can animals have similar emotions?
Scientists believe that elephants might.
When a herd member dies, elephants often stay beside the body for days.
Sometimes they cover the body with leaves or dirt.
It seems as if they are trying to bury it.
In Kenya, researchers saw elephants return to the place where a family member had died.
Even a year later, they stopped and touched the bones gently with their trunks.
But elephants also react to the bones of elephants they never knew.
They stop to smell and touch them, while ignoring other animal bones.
This suggests they can recognize death within their species.
We can’t be sure how elephants understand death.
However, their behavior shows that they respond to it with deep emotions.
Chapter 02 Reading 3 고양이 눈은 왜 밤에 빛날까?
Have you ever wondered why a cat’s eyes glow like tiny lights at night?
Inside a cat’s eye is a special layer called the tapetum lucidum.
It lies behind the retina, which senses light.
When light enters the eye, the tapetum lucidum reflects it back through the retina.
This lets the cat use the same light twice, so it sees better in the dark.
In fact, cats can see with only one-sixth the light humans need.
This reflection also makes a cat’s eyes shine.
The color of the glow can be different depending on the cat.
It can be green, yellow, or even blue.
In the 1930s, inventor Percy Shaw noticed this glow when a cat’s eyes reflected his car’s headlights on a foggy road.
It inspired him to create “cat’s eye” road reflectors.
These small glass bumps reflect headlights back, helping drivers see more safely at night.
Chapter 02 Reading 4 얼어붙어도 다시 살아나는 개구리
In winter, many animals hide or move to warmer places to escape the cold.
But the wood frog has a much more surprising way to survive.
It freezes solid!
Its heart stops and it does not breathe.
For weeks, it lies stiff like an ice cube, looking completely dead.
Then spring arrives, and the frozen frog slowly melts and comes back to life!
How is this possible?
Before winter, the wood frog fills its body with special chemicals.
These chemicals act like antifreeze and prevent ice crystals from forming inside the frog’s cells.
This protection keeps the cells from being damaged and allows the frog to live.
With this clever trick, the wood frog can survive the deep freeze that would kill most animals.
It is truly one of nature’s most amazing survivors.
Chapter 03 Reading 1 하늘을 나는 듯했던 무용수, 발레의 규칙을 깨다
Vaslav Nijinsky was a famous ballet dancer from Russia.
He became well known in the early 1900s for his great skill.
Audiences were amazed by his high jumps and fast spins.
Some even said he looked like he was flying.
Nijinsky was not just a dancer, though.
He was also a choreographer who created new kinds of ballet.
One of his most famous works was The Rite of Spring.
In traditional ballet, dancers moved gracefully to smooth, soft music.
But this piece broke all the rules.
The dancers moved with heavy steps and rough, sudden movements.
The music was loud and full of strange rhythms.
It was something people had never seen before.
Many people did not understand Nijinsky's style at the time.
However, his bold ideas later helped shape modern ballet.
Chapter 03 Reading 2 소리를 듣지 못한 작곡가는 왜 피아노 다리를 잘랐을까?
What would it be like if you couldn't hear music at all?
Ludwig van Beethoven faced this challenge when he wrote his Ninth Symphony.
At that time, he was completely deaf.
But instead of giving up, he found a way to feel the music.
He cut off the legs of his piano and placed it on the floor.
This way, he could feel the sound through vibrations from the floor.
Despite his hearing loss, Beethoven created a symphony that changed music history.
The Ninth is over an hour long.
That's nearly twice as long as most symphonies of the time.
It's also the first symphony to include singing.
In the final part, a choir joins the orchestra to sing a piece called Ode to Joy.
Today, the Ninth Symphony is performed across the world, and is still considered one of Beethoven's greatest works.
Chapter 03 Reading 3 푸른빛 비밀을 품은 고려의 그릇
Goryeo celadon is a type of pottery from Korea's past.
In Korean, it is called cheongja.
It was mainly made between the late 10th and 14th centuries, during the Goryeo Dynasty.
Celadon items included bowls, cups, and even roof tiles.
The most famous feature is its soft blue-green color.
This color was made by a special firing method using very little oxygen.
Goryeo potters mastered this technique and created a beautiful color.
But color was not the only special thing about celadon.
It also used a decoration technique called sanggam.
Instead of drawing, potters carved patterns into the clay.
Then they filled the patterns with colored clay before firing.
Goryeo potters were the first to use this technique on ceramics.
Goryeo celadon later influenced pottery across Asia.
It remains an important part of Korean tradition and culture.
Chapter 03 Reading 4 오페라와 뮤지컬, 무엇이 다를까?
Opera and musical theater are both live stage performances.
They combine music, acting, and storytelling.
But they do this in very different ways.
Opera began in Europe hundreds of years ago.
It focuses on classical music.
Singers use their powerful voices instead of microphones to fill the theater.
Almost every word is sung, while the orchestra creates the mood of each scene.
Musicals, on the other hand, are a more modern form of theater.
They mix spoken lines with songs and dance.
Singers usually use microphones, and the music can include pop, jazz, or rock.
The sets are colorful and change often.
In short, opera highlights classical music and voice, while musicals blend many art forms.
Their styles may differ, but both move the audience through story and song.
Chapter 04 Reading 1 언덕에서 치즈를 쫓아 구르는 사람들
Each spring near Gloucester, England, crowds gather for a strange and exciting race.
It's called the Cooper's Hill Cheese Rolling Competition.
From the top of Cooper's Hill, a large round cheese is rolled down.
Then participants chase after it as fast as they can.
The hill is so steep that they usually end up tumbling and sliding down rather than running.
Catching the cheese would be almost impossible and very dangerous.
So, the goal isn't actually to catch the cheese.
Instead, the first person to cross the finish line is the winner and gets the cheese as a prize.
This wild event is believed to be over 600 years old.
Some say it may have started as part of ancient spring celebrations.
No one knows exactly how it began.
However, it continues to be one of England's most unusual traditions.
Chapter 04 Reading 2 왕이 아내를 위해 지은 하얀 무덤의 비밀
In 1631, Shah Jahan, the king of India, faced a great sadness.
His wife, Mumtaz Mahal, died while having a baby.
To honor her, he built a grand tomb, now known as the Taj Mahal.
The Taj Mahal is famous for its bright white marble.
This special stone reflects sunlight, so the building seems to change color during the day.
It looks pink in the morning, becomes white at noon, and appears golden at sunset.
Another well-known feature is its perfect symmetry.
The left and right sides of the building look exactly the same.
Even the gardens and pools follow this design.
This balance makes the Taj Mahal harmonious and beautiful.
Building the Taj Mahal took more than 20 years.
About 20,000 workers and artists worked on it.
It shows the rich history of Indian architecture and art.
Chapter 04 Reading 3 물고기도 식물도 살 수 없는 호수에서 둥둥 뜨는 이유
The Dead Sea is a special lake between Jordan and Israel.
It is famous for its very salty water.
The water is almost ten times saltier than the ocean.
The Dead Sea is a closed lake with no outlet.
Water from the Jordan River flows in, but it cannot flow out to any ocean.
Under the hot and dry climate, the water evaporates quickly, but the salt stays behind.
Over thousands of years, this repeated process has made the lake extremely salty.
This salty water creates several interesting results.
No fish or plants can survive there.
That is how the Dead Sea got its name.
The extra salt also lets people float easily without any effort, so many tourists visit to try this special experience.
The Dead Sea shows how nature can create a very unusual place.
Chapter 04 Reading 4 하늘에 떠 있는 마을이 사라지고 있다고?
Civita di Bagnoregio is an old village in Italy famous for its unique location.
It sits on top of steep cliffs, so from far away, the village looks like it is floating in the sky.
To get to Civita, you must walk across a long bridge.
It is the only way into the village.
Inside the village, the narrow streets and ancient stone houses make you feel like you are traveling back in time.
Despite its beauty, Civita is often called “the dying village.”
The cliffs are made of soft rock, so they break down easily from rain and wind.
As the land is slowly falling apart, parts of the village are disappearing bit by bit.
People are trying to protect and repair the village.
They hope these efforts will keep Civita standing for a long time.
Chapter 05 Reading 1 산불이 난 숲을 하늘에서 되살린 형제의 아이디어는?
After a wildfire, planting trees by hand can take years.
Cameron and Bryce Jones, two brothers from Canada, wanted to find a faster way to replant forests.
In 2019, they came up with a bold idea.
They imagined drones that could plant trees from the sky!
The brothers started a company called Flash Forest.
With a team of engineers and scientists, they built drones that drop special seed pods.
Each pod holds a tree seed, plant food, and helpful fungi.
When the pod meets water, it breaks down naturally.
From there, the seed can sprout and grow into a tree.
The drones can plant thousands of trees in just one day, even in hard-to-reach places.
Thanks to this, the Jones brothers have already planted over 2.9 million trees all over the world.
Their work gives new hope to our planet’s forests.
Chapter 05 Reading 2 추락하던 엘리베이터를 멈춘 발명가의 한 수는?
In the early 1800s, elevators were mainly used in factories and warehouses to lift heavy goods.
They were simple platforms held up by ropes.
If a rope broke, the elevator crashed.
Because of this, people were afraid to use them.
This serious problem was solved by American inventor Elisha Otis.
In 1853, he invented the safety brake.
His device used special springs and hooks on the sides of the elevator.
When a rope broke, the springs pushed the hooks out.
The hooks then grabbed the side rails and stopped the elevator.
To prove it was safe, Otis gave a public demonstration.
He stood on the elevator and ordered the rope to be cut.
The brake worked and the elevator stopped immediately.
This success finally made people trust elevators.
With Otis’s invention, tall buildings became possible, and modern cities began to rise.
Chapter 05 Reading 3 문학상을 받은 가수, 그 이유는?
Most Nobel Prizes in Literature go to people who write books or poems.
However, in 2016, the world was surprised when one was given to American musician Bob Dylan.
Dylan became famous in the 1960s, a time of war and protest in the U.S.
These events influenced his music.
He used poetic language to write songs about freedom, peace, and justice.
His music reflected the social changes of the time and gave people hope.
The Nobel Committee said Dylan created new poetic expressions in the American song tradition.
This is why they gave him the prize.
Some critics argued that song lyrics are different from literature.
However, others supported the decision.
They said his meaningful lyrics were like modern poetry.
Dylan’s award showed that literature is not only written in books.
It can also be sung and felt through music.
Chapter 05 Reading 4 사고로 누운 침대에서 시작된 그림, 어떻게 위대한 예술이 되었나?
In 1925, when Frida Kahlo was eighteen, a terrible bus accident changed her life forever.
The crash broke her spine and forced her to stay in bed for months.
During those long, painful days, she began to paint to pass the time.
She painted herself, the subject she knew best.
Over time, Frida’s body healed.
But the pain from her injuries never went away completely.
Still, she kept painting.
Her self-portraits became a way for her to express her inner world.
She used bright colors and strong symbols to show her pain and emotions.
In this way, she revealed the strength she carried throughout her life.
Her honest works inspired many people who faced their own challenges.
By turning her suffering into powerful art, Frida became one of the great artists of the 20th century.
Chapter 06 Reading 1 몸속을 돌아다니는 아주 작은 센서의 정체는?
Nanomedicine is a new medical field that uses incredibly tiny materials to treat and prevent diseases.
These materials are called nanoparticles.
They are thousands of times smaller than a grain of sand.
They can move through the human body, even inside the bloodstream.
Nanoparticles act like tiny sensors.
They can detect very small changes in cells.
When they notice something unusual, they glow.
Doctors can see these signals on a screen clearly.
This helps doctors find early signs of disease, sometimes even before symptoms appear.
Nanoparticles also deliver medicine directly to diseased cells without harming healthy ones.
This makes treatments more effective and reduces side effects.
Scientists are still studying nanomedicine.
They believe it will lead to better treatments in the future.
Chapter 06 Reading 2 운동하기 가장 좋은 시간, 아침일까 저녁일까?
Have you ever wondered when the best time to exercise is?
Let’s see how the time you work out affects your body.
Morning workouts set a positive tone for the day.
They also increase your body’s energy use, helping you burn more calories throughout the day.
This supports weight loss and keeps you energized.
Afternoon is the perfect time for intense workouts.
Between 3 and 6 p.m., your body temperature rises, and your muscles become activated.
This state lowers the risk of injury and helps you get better results from your training.
Evening workouts can ease stress after a long day.
They help your body and mind relax.
This can improve your sleep quality.
In short, each time of day offers different benefits.
So the best time to exercise depends on your body and goals.
Chapter 06 Reading 3 운동선수들이 몸에 걸치는 작은 기기는 무엇을 알려 줄까?
Athletes wear small electronic devices called wearables during games or training.
These are helpful for professional athletes today.
They record valuable data on their bodies and performance.
This data can be used to improve performance.
For example, soccer players wear GPS vests.
These track how fast and how far they run.
Basketball players use smart shoes to measure how high they jump.
In tennis, sensors on rackets measure how fast a player swings.
Coaches look at these details to make training plans for each athlete.
Wearables also help prevent injuries.
They track changes in an athlete’s movement or heart rate.
These changes can show early signs of tiredness or injury.
If these signs appear, coaches can change training or let athletes rest.
With this technology, athletes can stay safe and play their best.
Chapter 06 Reading 4 설탕이 없는데 달콤한 음료, 정말 괜찮을까?
Many people enjoy soda, but they worry about too much sugar.
That’s why some choose zero-calorie drinks.
But how can they taste sweet with no sugar?
These drinks use artificial sweeteners instead of real sugar.
The sweeteners are much sweeter, so only a tiny amount is needed.
This small quantity adds almost no calories.
This is why the drink can be labeled “zero-calorie.”
Zero-calorie drinks may seem like a healthy choice.
However, some researchers warn about side effects.
They suggest that artificial sweeteners might confuse the brain’s sense of sweetness.
This can make people want more sweet food or affect how the body controls sugar.
Over time, these effects could cause health problems.
Zero-calorie drinks can help people avoid sugar, but they’re not a perfect solution.
So, it’s better not to rely on them too much.
Chapter 07 Reading 1 책 70권을 싣고 강을 건너는 당나귀 도서관
Many remote villages in Colombia do not have schools or libraries.
This means children don’t have access to books.
So Luis Soriano, a teacher in one of these areas, started a traveling library.
He called it Biblioburro, which means “donkey library” in Spanish.
With two donkeys and just 70 books, Luis began visiting small villages.
Each week, Luis and his donkeys travel up to 10 kilometers.
They cross rivers and climb narrow trails.
Children gather when the donkeys arrive.
Luis reads to them and lets them borrow books to take home.
Now, Biblioburro has more than 4,000 books.
A small library has also opened in Luis’s town.
His idea has helped many children enjoy reading and inspired others to start mobile libraries.
Chapter 07 Reading 2 교실이 바다 위에 있다면?
What if your classroom was on the sea?
That’s what happens when you join Semester at Sea.
It’s a college program where students travel and study on a ship.
The journey lasts about 100 days and stops in more than 10 countries.
While the ship is sailing, students take classes such as world history and international business.
The subjects they study depend on their majors or interests.
Some lessons also introduce the culture or history of the next country they will visit.
When the ship arrives at a port, students continue learning through real experiences.
Each student joins different activities related to their classes.
A history student might explore ancient ruins.
On the other hand, a business student could visit a local company.
For these students, the ocean is a campus, and every country is a classroom.
Chapter 07 Reading 3 토마토 타이머가 집중력을 살려 준다고?
In the 1980s, an Italian student named Francesco Cirillo had trouble focusing while studying.
One day, he grabbed a tomato-shaped timer and challenged himself to study for just two minutes.
Surprisingly, it worked!
He slowly increased the time and found that 25 minutes of study followed by a 5-minute break worked best.
He called each 25-minute study period a pomodoro, the Italian word for tomato.
This idea became the Pomodoro Technique.
It follows a simple pattern.
Study for 25 minutes, then rest for 5 minutes, and repeat.
After four of these sessions, take a longer break of 15 to 30 minutes.
This rhythm helps your brain stay focused without getting tired.
You also stay motivated as you finish each session.
Why not give it a try?
All you need is a timer!
Chapter 07 Reading 4 지루한 공부를 게임처럼 만드는 비밀
Gamification adds game-like features to everyday tasks.
It makes boring activities more exciting and enjoyable.
The language app Duolingo shows how gamification works in learning.
It uses short and fun lessons, like quick rounds in a game.
Learners earn points and badges when they learn new words or grammar.
They can also compete with other users to see who studies the most.
These fun challenges and rewards make learners want to study more.
Studies show that gamification helps students stay motivated.
They also show that students remember new information more easily.
Because of these benefits, gamification is spreading beyond apps.
Many schools now use it in subjects such as math and science.
This way keeps students interested in learning and helps them learn better.
Chapter 08 Reading 1 산에 가면 마음이 편해지는 진짜 이유
When you visit the mountains, the fresh air and trees help your mind relax.
This isn’t just a feeling.
Studies show that spending time in nature changes the chemicals in our bodies.
It can lower cortisol, the hormone related to stress.
It can also increase serotonin, which helps us feel calm and happy.
These changes slow our heart rate and make us feel more comfortable.
Scientists believe this reaction comes from our past.
Long ago, early humans searched for forests and grasslands to find food, water, and shelter.
These places increased their chance of survival.
Over time, humans began to connect green spaces with comfort and safety.
Because of this, we still respond positively to nature today.
So if you’re feeling stressed, take a moment to go outside.
Even a short time in nature can help you feel better.
Chapter 08 Reading 2 피처럼 붉은 액체가 나오는 소코트라의 나무
On the island of Socotra, off the coast of Yemen, there is a very unusual tree.
It has a wide top that looks like a huge upside-down umbrella.
This strange shape is a clever survival trick in the dry climate.
It helps the tree catch water from rain and fog and carry it to the roots.
But the tree is famous for another reason.
If its bark is cut, thick red liquid comes out.
Because this sap looks like blood, people named it the Dragon’s Blood Tree.
The red sap hardens and protects wounds on the bark.
It also has special chemicals that help the tree fight germs and keep insects away.
This tree is also known for its incredible age.
Many Dragon’s Blood Trees are hundreds of years old.
They stand as living symbols of Socotra’s ancient past.
Chapter 08 Reading 3 숲속에 숨은 인터넷, 우드 와이드 웹
Even though trees cannot walk or talk, they find ways to help each other.
There is a network of fungi underground that connects tree roots and allows them to communicate.
Scientists call it the “wood wide web.”
Through this network, trees can share water, food, and messages.
For example, if bugs attack one tree, it sends chemical signals through its roots.
Other trees detect these signals and start making bad-tasting chemicals in their leaves.
This helps keep the bugs away.
The network also allows big trees to help small ones.
In shady places, young trees cannot make enough food from sunlight.
Older trees send them nutrients through the network.
Without this help, many young trees would not survive.
We cannot see this network with our eyes.
However, it actively sustains the whole forest underground.
Chapter 08 Reading 4 초콜릿이 사라질지도 모른다고?
Chocolate is one of the world’s most popular treats.
But in the future, it might not be so easy to enjoy.
Chocolate comes from cacao trees, which grow in hot, rainy regions like West Africa.
These regions once had steady rainfall and stable temperatures.
But now, the climate is changing.
Rainfall is less regular and temperatures are rising.
Too little rain dries out the trees.
Too much damages the roots and spreads infection.
A temperature rise of just 2 degrees can stop cacao flowers from growing.
As a result, many trees are producing fewer cacao pods.
This affects both chocolate production and the farmers who rely on cacao for their income.
To help, scientists are developing stronger cacao trees.
These trees can grow well in this changing weather.
Also, some farmers are moving their crops to cooler hillsides with more stable conditions.
These efforts are just beginning.
Still, they give hope for chocolate’s future.
Chapter 09 Reading 1 뱀파이어는 어떻게 진짜가 되었을까?
Today, vampires are just fun characters in books and movies.
But long ago, many people believed they were real.
In Eastern Europe in the 1700s, terrible diseases spread, but no one knew why.
When people died suddenly, fear filled the villages.
The villagers suspected the dead could return and harm the living.
So they dug up graves to look for proof.
The villagers often saw blood near a dead person’s mouth or hair and nails that looked longer.
They didn’t know these were normal changes after death.
Instead, they thought the dead had come back to life.
The villagers called these “living dead” vampires.
To stop them, villagers burned the bodies or put stakes into their hearts.
These stories about vampires soon spread across Europe.
Later, science explained what really happened, and people realized vampires weren’t real.
But even today, the idea of vampires still fascinates us.
Chapter 09 Reading 2 괴물이 된 아름다운 여인, 메두사의 진짜 이야기
Most people know Medusa as a frightening monster.
In Greek mythology, however, she was once a beautiful woman.
One day, she angered the goddess Athena, and everything changed.
As punishment, Athena turned her hair into snakes and gave her a deadly gaze.
Anyone who looked at Medusa would turn into stone.
No one dared to look at Medusa, but the hero Perseus found a clever way.
He used his shiny shield like a mirror and watched her reflection.
This way, he could move close and kill her without looking at her directly.
Even after her death, Medusa’s power remained strong.
Perseus used her head to turn enemies into stone.
Later, he gave the head to Athena, and she placed it on her shield for protection.
From then on, Medusa’s image changed from a symbol of fear into one of strength and protection.
Chapter 09 Reading 3 발자국 하나가 만든 전설, 빅풋
For hundreds of years, Native American stories told of large, hairy men living deep in the mountains.
These mysterious creatures were called “Mountain Devils.”
Until the 1950s, these stories stayed mostly within Native American communities.
Then public interest grew sharply in 1958, when a road worker in California discovered huge footprints about 40 centimeters long.
People believed they were from a giant creature.
That’s how the name “Bigfoot” was born.
Later, some said that they saw a tall, smelly figure covered in long brown hair.
But no one ever caught it.
Since then, many people have searched for proof of Bigfoot.
Nowadays, they even use tools like special cameras.
No clear evidence has been found yet.
But people still venture into forests to discover the truth behind the legend.
Chapter 09 Reading 4 허풍 이야기가 힘든 하루를 버티게 한 이유
In the 1800s, many Americans moved west to start new lives on the frontier.
Life was rough and lonely, with hard work and harsh weather.
To cheer themselves up, settlers told tall tales about giant heroes.
One famous hero was Paul Bunyan, a huge lumberjack.
He was so tall that trees looked like grass beside him.
His footsteps left holes that became ponds.
He traveled with Babe, his blue ox.
People said that the land changed shape wherever they went.
According to one story, Paul walked across the Arizona desert, dragging his giant ax.
With each step, the blade cut into the dry ground.
After hundreds of miles, this deep cut became what we now call the Grand Canyon.
Of course, this never really happened.
But these tall tales gave settlers something to laugh about and helped them face another hard day.
Chapter 10 Reading 1 선수 뒤에서 뛰는 사람, 스포츠 에이전트
If you love sports, becoming a sports agent could be a great job.
Agents help athletes in many ways off the field.
They deal with player contracts, arrange transfers between teams, and find sponsors.
Agents also manage a player’s social media and public image.
This lets players focus only on training and games.
To become a sports agent, it is good to study sports management, business, or law.
It is important to be good at talking with people and making deals.
Also, in some sports, like soccer, agents must pass an exam.
They need to get a license before they can work.
Being a sports agent takes knowledge and effort.
But for those who love sports, it can be an enjoyable job.
Chapter 10 Reading 2 팔이 없어도 활을 쏘는 사람들
Para archery is a sport for people with physical disabilities.
It is similar to Olympic archery, but Para archers play in different ways.
Some archers shoot from wheelchairs, and some archers stand.
Others who cannot use their arms even shoot with their feet.
Special tools are also allowed.
For example, some archers use a small tool to pull the bow with their teeth.
These tools help each archer shoot in a way that fits their body.
In this sport, players keep trying and never give up.
Matt Stutzman is a famous American archer.
He was born without arms, but he learned to shoot with his feet.
This skill helped him win medals in big competitions.
His story shows that anyone can reach their goals if they try.
Chapter 10 Reading 3 테니스 공이 인인지 아웃인지, 이제는 AI가 판정한다
In the past, all decisions in sports were made by human referees, so their judgments weren’t always perfect.
Sometimes mistakes caused unfair results and made players and fans upset.
To reduce this, sports now use AI technology.
For example, tennis uses an AI line-call system.
High-speed cameras follow the ball from many angles.
AI builds a 3D picture of its path and decides if it is “in” or “out.”
The result appears on the screen in seconds, so the game can continue quickly.
This helps make sports more accurate and fair.
However, AI cannot decide everything.
Some complex decisions still need a referee’s experience and understanding of the game.
For now, AI is used to help referees, not replace them.
Chapter 10 Reading 4 우리는 왜 약한 팀을 응원할까?
When two teams play, do you cheer for the one that’s winning or losing?
Many people cheer for the underdog, the team or player that is not expected to win.
In sports, this is called the underdog effect.
Cheering for underdogs is natural.
People like players who face hard situations and still try their best.
An underdog’s victory also feels special since it is unexpected.
This effect also helps players.
Underdogs usually feel less pressure, so they can play more freely.
Because others do not expect much from them, they also try harder to prove themselves.
All of this helps them focus better, work together, and sometimes surprise everyone by winning.
